claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations let component authors ship an upgrade path with the component itself; a migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.
The v1 example uses the legacy `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc` component, which creates a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and association, and an internet gateway.
Because the security group refers to the VPC's ID, replacing the VPC would require replacing the AWS security group too (per AWS CloudFormation docs on the security group VpcId property).
A replacement database does not automatically contain the old database's data.
The modern component is `awsx.ec2.Vpc`.
The third version removes AWSX and declares the resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
Across all three versions of the example, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.
Pulumi state records both physical resources and components; each record has a URN, and managed resources also have a provider ID.

Legacy AWSX wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components, modern AWSX removes those wrappers, and in the example the subnet's Pulumi name changes from `vpc-isolated-0` to `vpc-isolated-1`.
Pulumi aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when saved state remains compatible, but cannot remove component wrappers and transfer references.
Pulumi resource options accept a `stateMigrations` option for registering a migration callback, used together with an alias for the legacy component type.

The migration callback receives the old component's saved state followed by its children's state and returns `newState` (the complete replacement records) and `successors` (a map from each disappearing old URN to its replacement URN).
Entries in `successors` let the Pulumi engine update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack, keeping the security group's VPC reference valid after migration.

Pulumi runs multiple state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next; a legacy AWSX stack can upgrade directly to plain AWS, and after migrations run, callbacks return no result on later updates.
After a migration, Pulumi compares the new program with the migrated state and calls the provider for remaining changes; the example can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.
`pulumi preview` evaluates the state migration without saving it, and `pulumi up` saves the migrated state.

When users upgrade a component that registers a migration and run Pulumi, it runs the migration automatically as part of normal preview and update, without users writing the migration or editing stack state.
The example repository contains all three programs and the migration code, and the component state migrations guide covers the callback contract.
State migration callbacks (the Pulumi resource option) run during previews and updates when prior state exists.
State migration callbacks must be idempotent and return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
State migration callbacks rewrite state without performing provider operations.
A Pulumi component state migration is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.
A Pulumi component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings.
In a Pulumi component state migration result, each successor mapping connects an old URN omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, the Pulumi component state migration callback returns no result.
The Pulumi state migration option reference page at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/statemigrations/#callback-api explains the callback API.
State entries passed to component state migration callbacks use the checkpoint resource format, including fields such as urn, type, id, parent, provider, inputs, and outputs.
A state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using Pulumi update plans or targeted updates.
The restrictions on state-changing migration results (for update plans and targeted updates) do not require removing an already-applied migration.
